question: Which channel did the pill close?
explanation: Sulfonylureas close the beta-cell potassium channel, so insulin is released even when glucose is already low. The beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channel is the target; closing it depolarizes the cell and releases insulin and C-peptide together. A pancreatic sodium channel is not the sulfonylurea site. examTakeaway: Aminoglycosides bind the 30S subunit and misread mRNA, which is why they are bactericidal and also toxic to ear and kidney.
scenario: A 60-year-old man on gentamicin for a gram-negative bacteremia develops rising creatinine and new tinnitus. The organism was sensitive. He asks how one drug can kill bacteria and injure the ear.
question: Which bacterial target does gentamicin bind?
explanation: Aminoglycosides bind the 30S subunit and misread mRNA, which is why they are bactericidal and also toxic to ear and kidney. The 30S ribosomal subunit is the gentamicin target. The 50S ribosomal subunit is the macrolide and chloramphenicol site. DNA gyrase is the fluoroquinolone target. Cell-wall crosslinks are the beta-lactam and vancomycin targets. Dihydrofolate reductase is the trimethoprim target.
